order: The defending champion will bid for an unprecedented fourth straight gold medal in Saturday’s final at Toyota stadium against familiar foe Japan, who beat Uzbekistan, 9-8, on penalties after the match was locked at 1-1 at the end of extra time.
The Koreans have stand-in captain Eom Ji-sung to thank for reaching the final as he set up goals for Bae and Lee Young-jun.
OSAKA — South Korea’s Bae Jun-ho struck late as it came from behind to snatch a 2-1 victory over China on Wednesday and reach a record fourth successive Asian Games final in men’s soccer.

Defender Peng Xiao missed a golden chance to put the Chinese ahead for a second time in the 62nd minute when a poor clearing header landed at his feet right in front of goal but his low shot fizzed wide of the post.

Japan, runner-up in the last two Games, also had to rally from behind after Sardorbek Bakhromov scored early for Uzbekistan, with a Sena Ishibashi header in the 88th minute taking the match into extra time.
Bae volleyed home in the 82nd minute from next to the far post after latching onto a long, lofted cross from Eom, who stepped up to replace injured skipper Lee Gi-hyuk.
Uzbekistan’s bid for a first final since its sole title in Hiroshima 1994 ended when defender Kuvonchbek Khushvaktov was denied by the crossbar in the shootout. — Reuters
China bowed out from its first Games semifinals in 28 years with some regret, having gone one step further as Under-23 Asian Cup runner-up in January.
